analysis.title: CIO View: Investment grade
key_insights: UBS CIO holds an Attractive absolute view on investment grade bonds, with a relative preference of In line versus other fixed income segments. Yields are 6% in USD and 4.3% in EUR.
Core preference is short- to medium-duration IG. The rise in long-dated government yields allows selective duration extension through high-quality issuers, mainly intermediate maturities.

Global yields stayed elevated. They drifted lower through most of October until the inflation data reversed the move. The rise this year reflects a reassessment of policy rate expectations after the onset of the US-Iran conflict.
US IG spreads were 91bps as of 17 November, against a historical median of 129bps since 2010. The broad US IG index yields 5.99% and the European IG index 4.26%.

October US headline and core CPI came in above expectations at 3.7% y/y. Hawkish remarks from Fed Governor Christopher Waller pushed markets to price more than one hike in December and flattened the Treasury curve.

UBS says markets are too hawkish in pricing three additional hikes until July 2027. UBS expects a further 50bps of US tightening by 1Q27 and does not see a new tightening cycle like 2022. Higher policy rates alone are not credit-negative, and the growth outlook is the key determinant for credit.

Demand is robust. According to Bank of America data, US high-grade bond funds and ETFs took in about USD 418bn year-to-date, equal to 8.2% of AUM. Recent data show some moderation amid rate volatility and AI supply uncertainty.

US IG gross issuance reached about USD 1.98tr year-to-date, around 26% above the same period last year. Much of the increase is technology companies funding AI investment, which UBS expects to continue into 2027.

Hyperscaler bonds are about 4.7% of the US IG index. AI-related bonds trade about 68bps wider than the broader IG market after adjusting for ratings and maturity, reflecting concerns over capex scale, debt financing and AI returns. UBS thinks part of this risk premium may prove excessive.

Per BofA 3Q26 data, earnings growth for core US IG issuers excluding financials, energy and technology/AI accelerated to 9.4% y/y from 7.7% in 2Q. Revenue growth was 6.8% y/y against 7.3% in 2Q. Earnings growth across all listed US IG issuers was 25.5% y/y, driven by large technology and energy companies. Earnings surprise was 4.4% against 8.2% in 2Q.

Tight spreads limit further compression potential. Spreads could widen moderately as the market absorbs issuance and adjusts to rate expectations, but UBS does not expect a material deterioration in fundamentals in its base case.

Key risks are a meaningful slowdown or recession (partly offset by lower government yields), persistent inflation and further tightening, and continued heavy AI-related issuance causing supply indigestion.

sector_views.rationale: AI-related bonds trade about 68bps wider than broader IG on capex and debt financing concerns. UBS sees issuer selection as important and thinks some of the risk premium may be excessive.

BofA 3Q26 data: revenue growth for the same core group was 6.8% y/y against 7.3% in the prior quarter.
BofA 3Q26 data: earnings growth across all publicly listed US IG issuers was 25.5% y/y, heavily influenced by large technology and energy companies.
BofA 3Q26 data: results beat expectations by 4.4%, against 8.2% in 2Q.

UBS's own forecast. It is not seen as the start of a 2022-style cycle.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Well below the 129bps median since 2010, so compensation for credit risk is limited.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight short- to medium-duration investment grade bonds, with selective extension into high-quality intermediate-maturity IG issuers
trade_ideas.rationale: This offers the best balance between yield and interest rate risk, and the rise in long-dated yields allows selective duration extension.
trade_ideas.risk: Recession, persistent inflation with further tightening, and continued AI-related issuance causing supply indigestion.

risk_factors: A meaningful slowdown or outright recession, though falling government yields could offset much of the spread widening.
Persistent inflation and further monetary tightening, especially if higher rate volatility weighs on investor demand and corporate financing.
Continued elevated bond issuance, particularly from AI-related technology companies, which could cause periodic supply indigestion and moderately wider spreads.
vol_and_positioning: Elevated interest rate volatility and AI supply uncertainty have moderated recent demand for US high-grade bond funds and ETFs.
Hyperscaler bond supply caused indigestion and wider spreads this year. Hyperscalers are about 4.7% of the US IG index.
geopolitical: The US-Iran conflict is cited as the onset of the reassessment of policy rate expectations that has lifted yields this year.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have considerable financial flexibility, strong businesses and substantial earnings. Some of the added risk premium may prove excessive as financing uncertainty declines, and AI infrastructure spending should support operating cash flow over the medium term.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-related bonds trade about 68bps wider than broader IG on concerns about capex scale, reliance on debt financing and uncertain returns. Heavy issuance could keep causing supply indigestion and wider spreads.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An AI bust scenario in which AI stocks deflate would take the US IG spread target to 180bps by December 2027.
